newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - US T-bond vols steady with futures flat.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - US T-bond vols steady with futures flat.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. Treasury bond options ended near steady Wednesday, taking their cue from futures, which went out unchanged on the day after an early rally fizzled.
July options volatility was bid up early, to a high of 8.47 percent, before sliding back to finish at 8.27 percent, a slight increase from the previous day's settlement at 8.23 percent.
"We're in a steady to better grind in volatility," said one bond options floor analyst.
September volatility ended the session at 8.47 percent, essentially unchanged from Tuesday, and down from 8.50 percent hit earlier in the day.
June bond futures ended the day unchanged at 108-23.

A bias toward selling puts was seen in Treasury options, with one U.S. brokerage firm a noted seller of 1,500 September 10-year note puts in the 103-00 strike and another trading house selling 1,000 July 107-00 bond puts.

Options analysts said bond volatility would likely remain underpinned before the release next week of the U.S. employment report for May. Economic indicators to be released later this week, including the first-quarter U.S. gross domestic product revision on Friday, and early next week will keep market participants on their toes.
A dive below 108-00 in June futures could cause volatility to spike higher because the highest concentration of open interest is currently in the 108-00 puts, the floor analyst said.
In Eurodollars, September volatility rose 0.2 point to 9.0 percent and December was steady at 10.9 percent.
